counterfactual_missing_items: Echocardiogram (age 42): Normal aortic measurements, tricuspid aortic valve
MRA neck, brain, chest, and abdomen (age 43): Unremarkable, no evidence of aneurysms
decisive_items: Doughy skin with palpable bilateral piezogenic papules
Increased range of motion in elbows, hips, and knees with normal strength
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete and specific: it inherits R2's EDS evidence and adds the hypermobile subtype, fitting the Beighton score, generalized joint hypermobility, doughy skin, and piezogenic papules. R1 is the runner-up due to skeletal/ocular overlap but is contradicted by normal aortic measurements. R3 is contradicted by unremarkable aneurysm imaging. R2 is subsumed by C1 as a broader label without the required subtype.

rejected.why: Subsumed by C1; broad EDS label without the hypermobile subtype, so less complete.
Loeys-Dietz is contradicted by unremarkable MRA/no aneurysms and normal aortic measurements; lacks arterial tortuosity and characteristic craniofacial features.
